wiki.extract: Alofi is the capital of the island nation of Niue. With a population of 610 in 2022, Alofi is the second-smallest national capital by population. It consists of two villages: Alofi North and Alofi South. They collectively serve as the capital, but of the two, Alofi South hosts more government buildings, as many were moved to the southern part after Cyclone Heta.

landmarks.name: Talava Arches
landmarks.writeup: Natural limestone arches located on the southeastern coast, popular for scenic views.

wiki.extract: Niue is a small, oval island in the South Pacific Ocean, to the east of Tonga. It has an area of 260 square kilometres, and a coastline of 64 km. It claims an exclusive economic zone of 200 nautical miles, and a territorial sea of 12 nautical miles. It is one of world's largest coral islands.

landmarks.name: Limu Pools
landmarks.writeup: Natural rock pools ideal for swimming and snorkeling.

wiki.extract: Niue is a self-governing island country in free association with New Zealand. It is situated in the South Pacific Ocean, is part of Polynesia, and is predominantly inhabited by Polynesians. As one of the world's largest coral islands, Niue is nicknamed "The Rock", which comes from the traditional name "Rock of Polynesia".

food_writeup: Niuean cuisine features seafood, taro, coconut, and tropical fruits, with traditional dishes like 'umu' (earth oven cooked food) being central to local meals.
brief_history: Niue was settled by Polynesians around 900 AD. It became a British protectorate in 1900 and was annexed by New Zealand in 1901. Niue gained self-governing status in free association with New Zealand in 1974.
current_conflicts: Niue is currently peaceful with no known internal or external conflicts.

commentary.inflation_management: Niue is self-governing in free association with New Zealand, uses the New Zealand dollar, and has no monetary policy or IMF data. With around 1,700 residents, there is barely a price level to manage - nearly everything is imported, and inflation is whatever New Zealand's is plus freight. Aid, remittances and .nu domain revenues fund consumption; tourism is small but growing.
commentary.debt_management: Niue carries no meaningful sovereign debt; its 'fiscal policy' is allocating New Zealand aid, domain-name income and modest tourism receipts. The long-running dispute over control and revenue of the .nu internet domain is the closest thing to a sovereign-wealth question. Economic viability rests entirely on external support, which Wellington provides steadily.

key_events.event: COVID-19 border closure cut the nascent tourism sector; reopening was slow and cautious.
Ongoing dispute with Sweden's IIS foundation over control of the lucrative .nu domain.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: Niue will remain a subsidized microstate; the realistic goal is not growth but viability - keeping population from declining further through tourism, remote-work visas and domain income. New Zealand's backing is assured. Climate resilience for water and the single hospital-scale infrastructure is the practical agenda. Expect quiet stability, not economic takeoff.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
